1d53fd.evidence: Control: nc_api_url() at php/namecheap.php:5-12 accepts only a bool; the URL string is entirely from getenv('NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX_API_URL'/'NAMECHEAP_API_URL') with hardcoded Namecheap defaults (lines 7-11), and nc_call() at php/namecheap.php:23 calls curl_init(nc_api_url((bool)($creds['sandbox'] ?? false))). connect.php:14 maps use_sandbox POST field to a boolean via `(string)$_POST['use_sandbox'] === '1'` — no URL string from user input ever exists. Repo-wide rg over php/ shows the only curl_init sinks are namecheap.php:23 (nc_api_url), bootstrap.php:124 (fixed https://api.ipify.org), and mcp.php:10 (MAILCOW_API_URL env + internal path); no user field (username, api_key, client_ip, domain, JSON-RPC params, headers) reaches any URL. Dynamic: connect.php tested with use_sandbox=1 vs 0 — only operator-configured endpoints are contacted; neither is attacker-chosen.

4eb79b.evidence: Control: detect_public_ip() at php/bootstrap.php:117-139 has no user input — curl_init('https://api.ipify.org') is a hardcoded string on line 124. Triggered via GET /api/status.php pre-auth (response captured: HTTP 200, {"ok":true,"connected":false,"username":null,"sandbox":false,"csrf":"9c09...","mailcow_origin":"https://host.docker.internal","public_ip":"146.70.126.61"}). The response leaks: server egress IP, session CSRF token (session-bound, not a static secret), mailcow_origin built from HTTP_HOST (reflects the request, not new info). Cache file CRED_DIR/.publicip written with default perms (no chmod, unlike store_credentials which chmods to 0600) — inside CRED_DIR which store_credentials chmods to 0700; not an additional exposure beyond the pre-auth status.php disclosure itself. Assessed as info disclosure only.

49469a.evidence: Auth gate confirmed at php/mcp.php:107-114 (getenv('MAILCOW_API_KEY') → Bearer regex → hash_equals → json_err 401), executed before ALL method dispatch (initialize:129, notifications/:137, tools/call:144). Dynamic: POST initialize no auth → 401, wrong Bearer → 401, GET wrong Bearer → 401 (order: auth before POST check — wrong-key GET leaks only the 401 body, never the 405 method hint), tools/call no auth → 401, notifications/initialized no auth → 401. Proxy ids 18,19,20,28,29,91,92,33. hash_equals timing-safe; Bearer regex (multi-token 'Bearer x y' fails match → 401); empty/unset key short-circuits to 401 (verified live PHP 8.4 harness, fail-closed). Correct-key control passes gate (reaches 400 Invalid JSON-RPC), proving the gate is the only barrier. No BFLA/bypass found.

15c042.risk_area: XXE / entity expansion / DTD transclusion on upstream XML
15c042.evidence: Control: PHP's libxml2 >= 2.9 disables external entity loading by default. nc_call() at php/namecheap.php:39 parses with @simplexml_load_string($body) — no LIBXML_NOENT flag passed (the only flags bit used is default 0), so external entity resolution is off. Verified this runtime build: PHP 8.4.24 CLI in the sandbox with libxml 2.15.3 (LIBXML_VERSION=21503), simplexml external-entity file read against a real local canary returned empty content by default; adding LIBXML_NOENT fetched the canary content — proving the flag is what enables it and it is absent in namecheap.php. Dynamic local snippet: php /tmp/xxe_probe.php + /tmp/xxe_probe3.php. The XML body comes from an operator-configured endpoint (nc-mock:8088 in this deployment), not directly from attacker input; no DTD/parameter-entity transclusion path is enabled.

199d22.risk_area: Mass assignment / unrestricted attrs passthrough to mailcow edit/domain
199d22.evidence: php/mcp.php:97-102 forwards the caller's attrs object 1:1 as {'items':[$domain],'attr':$attrs} to mailcow POST /api/v1/edit/domain — no key allowlist (verified: no array_intersect_key in file). Dangerous keys ARE forwardable (active:"0", backupmx/relay_all_recipients:"1", maxquota/defquota overrides, rl_value/rl_frame per the tool description at line 69) — verified by encoding a hostile attrs payload. However the only caller must hold the read-write MAILCOW_API_KEY (php/mcp.php:112 gate), which could call mailcow's own admin API directly with identical effect — no privilege added, and the tool contract documents read/write domain management. Cannot dynamically confirm (no real key); assessed source-only within the trust boundary. Not a vulnerability by itself.

98b236.risk_area: Spoofed ClientIp / authz-trust on client-supplied IP
98b236.evidence: connect.php:13 reads user-supplied client_ip, validates with FILTER_VALIDATE_IP (400 on invalid), passes to nc_call as ClientIp param. detect_public_ip() only runs when client_ip is empty (connect.php:33-34). Server-side consequence: none — client_ip is never read back for any authz or trust decision; rg over php/ shows its only readers are nc_call param building (namecheap.php:12) and the IP-not-whitelisted error message construction (namecheap.php:44-46). Namecheap gates by the real source IP of the server, not this parameter. Attacker can claim any IP in the outbound call; assessed honestly as low/info.

9e3de8.evidence: php/domains.php:158 → require_namecheap_session() (bootstrap.php:85-96): empty($_SESSION['nc_connected']) → 401 'Not connected'; missing creds file → unset flags + 401 'Stored connection is gone' (no leak). Dynamic: GET /api/domains.php no cookie → 401 (proxy ids 83/84); POST → 405 method-first (id 87). Creds-file-gone path verified by reading (cannot touch /credentials). Cross-session global-creds risk is a connect.php-owned issue (threat model), not this endpoint's gate.

c4159d.risk_area: Object-level authz / domain parameter injection (SSRF-like smuggle to upstream API)
c4159d.evidence: php/dns.php:158 gates on require_namecheap_session() before any domain handling. Dynamic: no cookie → 401 (proxy ids 85/86, 9). Domain regex (php/dns.php:161, same pattern as mcp.php:86) validated with PHP 8.4 against 26 payloads — ALL rejected except benign: query smuggle (example.com?x=1), '-a- evil.com', '../etc/passwd', encoded traversal, null bytes, fragments, slashes, unicode raw, punycode-no-TLD, 64-char labels, 313-char names, cloud metadata IP, [::1], empty/leading labels, uppercase, trailing dot — all rejected. Legit punycode (xn--80ak6aa92e.com) and 63-char labels accepted; 4-label 253-char name ACCEPTED, 255 rejected (length boundary enforced). DomainName reaches Namecheap only post-regex (php/dns.php:165 → php/namecheap.php:85 passes ['DomainName' => $domain]). No injection/smuggle vector.

01d6a3.risk_area: XSS / reflected input injection via JSON-RPC id and unknown-tool echo
01d6a3.evidence: $payload['id'] and unknown-tool names echo verbatim into JSON responses (mcp.php:35-41, 149), but all responses flow through json_out() (bootstrap.php:21-29) with Content-Type application/json; charset=utf-8 + X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff + Cache-Control: no-store and json_encode — harness-replicated echo of id + tool name arrives as JSON strings, inert. nginx adds nosniff + X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN globally (landing.conf:193-195). Post-auth reflection probes blocked pre-auth (proxy ids 91/92 returned 401); harness-verified echo path. No XSS vector.

cff88b.risk_area: CSRF (token single-use / session-bound / timing-safe / cross-site forgeability)
cff88b.evidence: CSRF forgery blocked by hash_equals() compare of a 128-bit random token bound to the victim session (php/bootstrap.php:44-49), SameSite=Lax session cookie (bootstrap.php:8-16), and POST-only enforcement. Probes: valid token via header -> 200 (x3, token non-rotating but replay requires knowing it); attacker token + victim cookie -> 403; empty header -> 403; no cookie + no token -> 403; GET -> 405. No Origin/Referer check exists (residual defense-in-depth gap, noted).

ec3170.risk_area: CSRF (require_csrf gate placement vs rate limit; token single-use / session-bound / timing-safe)
ec3170.evidence: CSRF gate confirmed on this endpoint: POST /api/connect.php without any token -> 403 'Invalid CSRF token, reload the page'; require_csrf() runs BEFORE register_failed_attempt() per source (php/connect.php:9), so the gate is not affected by and does not burn the per-session rate limit. Same control set as disconnect.php (hash_equals + session-bound token + SameSite=Lax); forgery not demonstrated. Token non-rotating and pre-auth fetchable per-session (status.php) — residual risks noted in findings note 7fa3e2; session fixation is the compounding weakness (Session-Validator's scope).

fac892.evidence: GET /api/status.php returns the session csrf to any unauthenticated visitor: 32 hex chars (16 random bytes via bin2hex(random_bytes(16)), php/bootstrap.php:36-42), stored in $_SESSION — same cookie returns the same token (persistent, non-rotating), different cookie returns a different token. Set-Cookie: MULTIAI_LANDING=...; path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax (no Secure flag over plain HTTP). Pre-auth fetchability is session-scoped and harmless alone; compounding risk only with session fixation (documented in findings note 7fa3e2).

e6954a.risk_area: brute-force / rate-limit protection (per-session counter, no IP or global limiter)
e6954a.evidence: Dynamic PoC against live target: 6 bad connect attempts with one cookie jar → 401×5 then 429 "Too many failed attempts" on attempt 6 (per-session lockout works). Then 8 bad attempts with a fresh session each → all 401, zero 429 (limiter bypassed by cookie rotation). Static review of /workspace/landing/php (rg across bootstrap.php, connect.php, domains.php, dns.php, mcp.php, status.php, disconnect.php) confirms no IP-based or global limiter exists anywhere; attempts tracked only in $_SESSION['nc_attempts'] (bootstrap.php:98-108). Validation errors (400) occur before register_failed_attempt (connect.php:22-29), so only Namecheap-reaching attempts are counted; clear_failed_attempts() on success resets the counter. No valid Namecheap key was used — bad api_key formats rejected client-side, zero upstream guessing traffic.

8c53bc.risk_area: Session fixation (client-chosen session ID accepted, no ID rotation on authenticated transition)
8c53bc.evidence: Dynamic PoC against live target: GET /api/status.php with fixed cookie MULTIAI_LANDING=9cdc672410784680891ec7a3d76d84d4 returned 200 with Set-Cookie None (server accepted client-chosen session ID, use_strict_mode off) and minted csrf f0dc2a006b4f97bfc9cded8dc533d0b8 for that session; POST /api/connect.php with that csrf on the fixed session passed the CSRF gate (401 from the Namecheap call, not 403). Connect-success replay blocked — mock Namecheap host unreachable from test container. Filed as vuln-0002 with inline fix (strict mode + session_regenerate_id on transition).

ab61c3.risk_area: Cross-user credential overwrite / multi-tenant leakage (last-connector-wins global creds file)
ab61c3.evidence: Static conclusive mechanism from source: CRED_FILE is one global path (php/bootstrap.php:16-17); store_credentials() wholesale-overwrites it (bootstrap.php:52-64) and read_credentials() returns it to any connected session (bootstrap.php:66-76); connect.php:43-50 sets nc_connected without keying creds to the session. Pairable-session mechanism (client-chosen session IDs accepted) dynamically confirmed in vuln-0002 against the live target. Full A/B connect-success chain blocked — mock Namecheap host unreachable from test container. Filed as vuln-0003.

32b461.risk_area: Unauthenticated info disclosure (CSRF token, last connector's username, sandbox flag, public IP)
32b461.evidence: Dynamic PoC against live target: GET /api/status.php with no cookie returned 200 with fresh-session csrf 4af774d5e8a3124c70dd41576f8f7e9e, mailcow_origin https://host.docker.internal, and public_ip 146.70.126.61 (server egress IP via api.ipify.org); with a fixed cookie the same unauthenticated response returned a csrf token minted for an attacker-chosen session. Username was null in this run because no successful Namecheap connection existed in the shared store during the test window; the endpoint reads the last connector's username and sandbox flag from the global creds store whenever a connection exists (php/status.php:61-72). Filed as vuln-0004.
